title:
SplatAnything:
Gaussian Spacing Normalization for Feed-forward 3DGS across Arbitrary Scenes
abstract:
We identify a key limitation of existing feed-forward 3DGS methods: Gaussian attributes are typically predicted in a *radial-distance-normalized* space that canonicalizes a global radial statistic of the reconstructed geometry, while the spacing between neighboring Gaussian centers can still vary substantially across scene scales and camera configurations. This mismatch induces systematic shifts in Gaussian-scale targets, leading to ambiguous supervision.
To address this, we propose **SplatAnything** with *Gaussian Spacing Normalization (GSNorm)*, which canonicalizes a robust scene-level statistic of Gaussian spacing to provide a more consistent spatial reference for Gaussian prediction. To rigorously assess our method, we further establish a systematic benchmark spanning diverse datasets, input sparsity levels, and challenging extrapolated viewpoints. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SplatAnything achieves state-of-the-art performance, with particularly strong gains under substantial variations in scene scale and viewpoint.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.markdown:
Feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) directly predicts a 3D
Gaussian representation  from input images, avoiding
the costly per-scene optimization of conventional 3DGS.
This efficiency makes it attractive for large-scale 3D reconstruction and
digital content creation.
The ultimate goal is a single model that generalizes reliably across
arbitrary scene scales, camera configurations, and target viewpoints, yet
such broad generalization remains challenging.

A prevailing paradigm is to first predict per-pixel depth using a
geometry foundation model ,
and then predict per-pixel Gaussian attributes based on the resulting
geometry in its *radial-distance-normalized* coordinate space.
*Radial Distance Normalization (RDNorm)* uses the mean radial
distance of reconstructed 3D points to the reference-camera origin as a
scene-level scale, and globally rescales the scene to canonicalize this

sections.heading: Formulation
sections.markdown:
Given $N$ input images
$\mathcal{I}=\{I_{i}\}_{i=1}^{N}$,
together with optional camera intrinsics
$\mathcal{K}=\{K_{i}\}_{i=1}^{N}$
and extrinsics
$\mathcal{T}=\{(R_{i},t_{i})\}_{i=1}^{N}$,
our goal is to predict a 3D Gaussian scene representation

$$\mathcal{G}=\left\{\left(\mu_{j},\alpha_{j},\Sigma_{j},\mathrm{sh}_{j}\right)\right\}_{j=1}^{M},$$

where $\mu_{j}$, $\alpha_{j}$, $\Sigma_{j}$, and $\mathrm{sh}_{j}$
denotethe Gaussian center, opacity, covariance, and SH coefficients.

sections.heading: Training SplatAnything
sections.markdown:
The training datasets and view-sampling strategies are detailed in the
appendix.

Given a rendered target-view image $\hat{I}_{t}$ and its ground-truth
image $I_{t}$, we supervise the model using a pixel-wise MSE loss and an
LPIPS perceptual loss:

$$\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{MSE}}=\frac{1}{3HW}\left\|\hat{I}_{t}-I_{t}\right\|_{2}^{2},\qquad\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{LPIPS}}=\operatorname{LPIPS}\left(\hat{I}_{t},I_{t}\right).$$

The overall objective is

$$\mathcal{L}=\lambda_{\mathrm{MSE}}\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{MSE}}+\lambda_{\mathrm{LPIPS}}\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{LPIPS}},$$

where
$\lambda_{\mathrm{MSE}}=\lambda_{\mathrm{LPIPS}}=1$
in our implementation.

SplatAnything is trained for 20,000 iterations on 64 NVIDIA H20 GPUs,
using 4 to 32 input views and dynamically varying the input resolution
from 504 to 1024. We use a 500-step warm-up and learning rates of
$5\times 10^{-6}/2\times 10^{-5}$ for the

sections.heading: Evaluation Benchmark
sections.markdown:
Existing benchmarks are typically concentrated on a small set of datasets and evaluate interpolated target views, making it difficult to assess cross-domain and viewpoint generalization. To provide a more comprehensive evaluation, we design a new benchmark with the following properties:

**Cross-domain and cross-scale coverage.**
We evaluate on **seven datasets**: ScanNet , NRGBD , DL3DV , Tanks and Temples , Mip-NeRF 360 , ETH3D , and DTU . These datasets span a wide range of physical scene scales, providing a substantially broader test of cross-domain and cross-scale generalization.

**Controlled extrapolation and observation sparsity.**
We sample context views from a compact trajectory span and select target
views using an occlusion-aware symmetric co-visibility criterion.

sections.heading: Quantitative Comparisons
sections.markdown:
We report the average metrics over **4/8/16/32/64 input views** in Table 1, specific results under different input-view settings are provided in the appendix. Following SHARP , we primarily report *LPIPS* and *DISTS* in the main paper, as they better reflect rendering quality and higher-frequency details. We also report the results in the monocular setting in Table 6.
Overall, SplatAnything achieves the strongest performance across most datasets and evaluation settings, demonstrating its superior generalization capabilities.

sections.heading: Qualitative Comparisons
sections.markdown:
Figs. 5 and 6 present qualitative comparisons across diverse scenes and extrapolated viewpoints under multi-view and monocular input settings, covering object-centric captures, indoor environments, and large-scale outdoor scenes. **SplatAnything** demonstrates a significant advantage in rendering quality: it generalizes robustly across a wide range of scene types and spatial scales, maintains geometric consistency under challenging large viewpoint
extrapolation, and produces sharp, detailed renderings that faithfully recover fine local structures. More results are provided in the appendix.

sections.heading: Efficiency Analysis
sections.markdown: We evaluate the inference efficiency of **SplatAnything** and other methods under different input-view settings. Detailed timing results are provided in the appendix.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.markdown:
We identified a key limitation of existing methods: *Radial Distance
Normalization (RDNorm)* does not directly normalize Gaussian spacing,
leading to ambiguity in Gaussian-scale supervision across scene scales and
camera configurations. To address this issue, we introduced
**SplatAnything** with *Gaussian Spacing Normalization (GSNorm)*,
which derives a scene-level normalization factor from a representative
statistic of Gaussian spacing and provides a more consistent spatial
reference for Gaussian prediction. We further established a systematic
cross-dataset benchmark covering different input sparsity levels and
challenging extrapolated viewpoints. Experiments demonstrate that
SplatAnything achieves the strongest performance across most evaluation
settings, highlighting the effectiveness of GSNorm and marking a
substantial step toward feed-forward 3DGS.

sections.markdown:
We provide additional details of the evaluation benchmark introduced in
the main paper. Our benchmark spans seven datasets and evaluates different
input-view counts of $4$, $8$, $16$, $32$, and $64$. The protocol is
designed to independently control input-view sparsity and target-view
difficulty, while ensuring identical evaluation conditions across methods.

sections.heading: Inference Efficiency
sections.markdown: We measure the median forward-pass latency per scene for producing Gaussian attributes under different numbers of input views. As shown in Table 11, the runtime of all methods increases with the number of input views. SplatAnything remains substantially faster than computationally heavier baselines such as DA3-GS, QuerySplat, and TokenGS. All methods are infered on a single NVIDIA H20 GPU. Inference uses BF16 precision and a batch size of 1. All input images are resized to the same resolution of $448\times 896(H\times W)$ to match the input constraints of all methods.

sections.heading: Application to Panoramic 3D Content Generation.
sections.markdown:
We explore SplatAnything for panoramic-image-based 3D
content generation.
We use WorldPano  to generate a panoramic image and
convert it into cubemap perspective views with a
$95^{\circ}\times 100^{\circ}$ FoV, which remains substantially wider than
typical perspective inputs.
These views are fed directly into SplatAnything for 3D Gaussian
reconstruction.
As shown in Fig. 13, SplatAnything produces
high-quality novel-view synthesis under this
challenging wide-FoV setting.
These results demonstrate its robustness to substantially different
camera configurations and further highlight the potential of
SplatAnything as a general feed-forward 3DGS framework.

figures.label: Figure 1
figures.caption:
Given any number of input images and optional camera poses,
**SplatAnything** reconstructs a 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS)
representation within seconds. It generalizes across arbitrary scene
scales and camera configurations, while supporting challenging
extrapolated viewpoints. Compared with prior feed-forward 3DGS methods,
SplatAnything achieves substantially stronger cross-scene generalization
and novel-view rendering quality.

figures.label: Figure 2
figures.caption:
**Normalization space.**
(a) *Radial Distance Normalization* canonicalizes a global
radial statistic but leaves Gaussian spacing varying across scenes
and camera configurations, resulting in inconsistent
supervision targets.
(b) *Gaussian Spacing Normalization* canonicalizes a representative statistic of Gaussian spacing, providing a more consistent spatial reference for Gaussian prediction.

figures.label: Figure 3
figures.caption:
**Architecture of SplatAnything.**
Given $N$ input images and optional camera parameters,
a frozen geometry foundation model first estimates multi-view
geometry.
We convert the geometry from its native radial-distance-normalized
space to the proposed Gaussian-spacing-normalized space and predict
per-pixel Gaussian attribute through a Gaussian backbone and a lightweight GShead.
